title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk menyebutkan jenis cuaca dan pakaian yang dikenakan sehari-hari.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 80-82
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new words about the weather and the clothing we wear when the weather is cold.
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about cold and wet weather clothing.
Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about clothes and the weather using “will / won’t”, “so”, and “because”.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
Ask the class, “What’s the weather like today? Look out of the window.” Elicit some words (e.g. sunny, hot, cloudy, rainy) and write them on the board.
Play a quick mime game: the teacher acts out a type of weather (e.g. shivering with cold, fanning the face because it is hot, holding an umbrella in the rain) and students guess the weather word.
Invite 2-3 volunteers to mime a type of weather for the class to guess.
Other alternatives to warm up the class: hot potato and throw the ball (the student who catches the ball says one weather word).
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 80.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures (e.g. girls sitting in the snow, a girl with an umbrella, people sitting in the sun). Elicit some ideas from the group and write down any key words on the board.
Read the questions on the page together, e.g. “What do you wear or carry with you when it is cold and wet outside? What about when it’s sunny?” and “Do you like sunny or rainy weather? Why?”

The teacher can model his/her own answers first, e.g. “When it is raining, I carry an umbrella.” or “I like sunny weather because I can go for a walk with my friends.” Write them on the board or show them on the screen.
Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but if they don’t have enough vocabulary, it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.
After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students. Tell them that by the end of Unit 10 they will be able to answer questions like these more easily.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 81 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear the words in the audio.

Before playing the audio, read all of the words together: wet weather, cloudy, waterproof boots, a heavy coat, thick gloves, a long-sleeved shirt, a knitted scarf, a woolen sweater. Ask simple questions to check understanding, e.g. “What do we wear on our hands?”
Play audio 10.1. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs (e.g. “Eric puts on a heavy coat to stay warm in the cold and windy weather.”).
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.

Play audio 10.2 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio. Check to make sure all students are repeating the vocabulary.
Pay attention to the pronunciation of the compound words such as long-sleeved shirt, waterproof boots, and woolen sweater.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc. Repeat the activity if needed.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task on page 81 and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do (Answer: long-sleeved shirt).
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the task in around 5 minutes, using the vocabulary from Vocabulary A.
Then, check the answers. Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book. Note that number 5 can be answered in either order (woolen sweater / heavy coat).
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Write one question for each new word on the board or show them on a screen, for example:
When do you usually wear a woolen sweater?
What do you do when the weather is wet?
Do you prefer wearing a long-sleeved shirt or a T-shirt?
What do you like to do on a cloudy day?
Do you have waterproof boots for rainy days?
Ask students to write the questions in their notebooks. Put students in pairs and tell them to take turns asking and answering the questions, writing their partner’s answers in their notebooks.
Elicit answers from the class or ask some students to write their answer to one question on the board (e.g. “I wear a woolen sweater when it’s cold.”). Correct any mistakes together as a class.
Put students in new pairs and ask them to repeat the activity.
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 82.
First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.

Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Read with a friend). Encourage students to change the key vocabulary by using the clothing and weather words learned on page 81.

Highlight the meaning of the connectors: “so” shows a result (The weather will be cloudy today, so I will wear jeans.) and “because” gives a reason (I will wear a heavy coat because the weather will be cold.).

Point out common mistakes, e.g. “I wear a coat tomorrow” instead of “I will wear a coat tomorrow”, “I won’t wearing shorts” instead of “I won’t wear shorts”, and using “because” and “so” in the same sentence.
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at the practice task on Student Book page 82 and ask some instruction-checking questions.
Read the example aloud together as a class. Then, read the questions aloud together as a class.

Tell students to complete the answers following the example, using will / won’t, so / because, and a time expression (e.g. tomorrow, on Friday). Remind them to use the Language Box at the bottom of the page to help guide them.
Students work in pairs or individually for around 6-8 minutes. Then put them in new pairs to compare their answers.
Check the answers. Write the answers on the board (e.g. 1. will be / so / will wear / won’t wear). Ask students to correct their answers if they are wrong.
Ask students to take turns reading the questions and answers aloud together. Student A asks the questions first, and then Student B answers them. Then switch the roles.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Write the questions below on the board or show them on a screen:
What will you wear tomorrow? Why?
What won’t you wear tomorrow? Why not?
What will you wear on Saturday? Why?
What won’t you wear on Saturday? Why not?
Also write the sentence starters: “The weather will be … so I will wear …” and “I will wear … because the weather will be …”.
Put students in pairs and ask them to practice asking and answering the questions, using two or more clothing items in each answer.

For review, the teacher can also ask “Why” questions about the last unit on vacations, e.g. “Why do you like going to the beach?” – “I like going to the beach because I like to read in the sun.” / “I like to read in the sun, so I like going to the beach.”
Elicit some answers from the class and give feedback on the use of so and because.
Choose 1-2 students to say what they will wear tomorrow and why, using “so” or “because” (e.g. “It will be rainy tomorrow, so I will wear waterproof boots.”).
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
